description: Alanine aminotransferase is an intracellular enzyme found predominantly in hepatocytes (liver cells). Upon cellular injury or membrane damage, ALT spills into the systemic circulation.
what_it_measures: Measures hepatocellular injury with high specificity for liver parenchymal damage.

clinical_significance.elevated_alt: Marked elevations (> 10-20 times normal) occur in acute viral hepatitis (A, B, C, E), acetaminophen/drug toxicity, or ischemic hepatitis (shock liver). Moderate elevations occur in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (MASLD), alcoholic hepatitis, and cirrhosis.

description: Aspartate aminotransferase is found in liver tissue, cardiac muscle, skeletal muscle, kidneys, and brain.
what_it_measures: Measures cellular damage in liver, myocardium, or skeletal muscle.

clinical_significance.ast_alt_ratio: An AST/ALT ratio > 2:1 strongly suggests alcoholic liver disease. An AST/ALT ratio < 1 is typical of viral hepatitis and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Isolated AST elevation without ALT often points to myocardial or skeletal muscle injury (rhabdomyolysis).

description: Bilirubin is an orange-yellow pigment produced by normal heme breakdown from senescent red blood cells, processed and conjugated in the liver, and excreted via bile into the gut.
what_it_measures: Evaluates liver excretory function, biliary patency, and hemolysis.

clinical_significance.jaundice: Elevations above 2.5 - 3.0 mg/dL produce clinical jaundice (yellow sclera and skin). Unconjugated/indirect hyperbilirubinemia indicates hemolysis or Gilbert syndrome; conjugated/direct hyperbilirubinemia indicates biliary obstruction (gallstones, stricture, pancreatic tumor) or viral/drug hepatitis.

description: TSH is a glycoprotein hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland that directs the thyroid gland to synthesize and release thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Regulated by negative feedback.
what_it_measures: Primary first-line screening biomarker for thyroid gland dysfunction.

clinical_significance.elevated_tsh: Indicates primary hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's autoimmune thyroiditis, iodine deficiency, post-thyroidectomy). Pituitary pumps out excess TSH to stimulate failing thyroid. Symptoms: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, bradycardia.
clinical_significance.suppressed_low_tsh: Indicates hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease, toxic multinodular goiter, thyroiditis) or excess exogenous levothyroxine replacement. Symptoms: weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, anxiety, palpitations, diarrhea.

description: Free T4 is the unbound, biologically active fraction of the primary hormone thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland.
what_it_measures: Measures active unbound thyroxine circulating in blood, unaffected by changes in binding proteins.

clinical_significance.low_ft4_with_high_tsh: Definitive diagnosis of overt primary hypothyroidism.
clinical_significance.high_ft4_with_low_tsh: Definitive diagnosis of overt hyperthyroidism / thyrotoxicosis.
clinical_significance.normal_ft4_with_abnormal_tsh: Subclinical thyroid dysfunction (subclinical hypothyroidism or subclinical hyperthyroidism).
